title: Auto Electrician Salary: Award Rates, Median Pay, and How to Calculate Your Annual Income
description: Learn how to calculate an auto electrician salary from hourly rates, including award minimums, median earnings, casual loading, super, and tax. Use our free timesheet tool.
salarySummary: Based on the Fair Work Ombudsman award, an auto electrician (Electrical worker grade 5) earns a minimum of $29.45 per hour, or $1,119.10 per week for 38 hours, while the median full-time auto electrician earns $2,808 per week (49 hours) according to Jobs and Skills Australia.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for an auto electrician under the award?
faqs.a: Under the Electrical, Electronic and Communications Contracting Award 2020, an auto electrician classified as an Electrical worker grade 5 has a minimum hourly rate of $29.45 (from 1 July 2026). This rate applies to full-time and part-time employees before any casual loading. For casual employees, the rate is $36.81 per hour (including 25% casual loading). The award also includes allowances for tools, licences, and leading hand duties.

faqs.q: How does the median auto electrician salary compare to the award minimum?
faqs.a: According to Jobs and Skills Australia (ABS data, May 2025), the median full-time auto electrician earns $2,808 per week, which is $46 per hour based on a 49-hour average week. This is significantly higher than the award minimum of $29.45 per hour, reflecting market premiums for experience, qualifications, and overtime. However, the award rate is the legal minimum; actual pay can vary by employer and location.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual auto electrician salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Use the formula: annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For example, at the award minimum of $29.45 per hour for 38 hours: $29.45 × 38 × 52 = $58,193.20 per year. If you work 49 hours (the median), annual gross would be $29.45 × 49 × 52 = $75,038.60. Remember to add super (12% on top) and deduct tax using the 2026–27 resident rates. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool can do this for you.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding an Auto Electrician Salary

If you're looking up an **auto electrician salary**, you'll find a wide range depending on whether you're paid the award minimum or the market median. Auto electricians install, maintain and repair electrical wiring and electronic components in motor vehicles. Their pay is covered by the *Electrical, Electronic and Communications Contracting Award 2020*, which sets minimum rates, allowances, and conditions. However, many experienced auto electricians earn well above the award due to demand and overtime.

This guide explains how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, what the award says, what the latest ABS data shows, and how casual loading, super, and tax affect your take-home pay.

### The Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard way to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a 38-hour week for full-time award employees, as that is the ordinary hours under the award. If you work more hours (e.g., 49 hours, the average for auto electricians), adjust the formula accordingly. The result is an estimate – it does not include overtime penalties, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For a precise calculation, use our [the timesheet](/) tool.

### Award Minimum Rates for Auto Electricians

The Fair Work Ombudsman's award classifies electrical workers from Grade 1 to Grade 10. An auto electrician typically falls under Grade 5 (qualified tradesperson). From 1 July 2026, the minimum rates are:

| Classification | Minimum weekly rate (38 hours) | Minimum hourly rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Electrical worker grade 5 | $1,119.10 | $29.45 |
| Electrical worker grade 8 (advanced) | $1,283.10 | $33.77 |

These are the base rates for full-time and part-time employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, so a Grade 5 casual would earn $36.81 per hour. The award also includes allowances for tools, electrician's licence, and leading hand duties – these are added to the base rate for all purposes (overtime, leave, etc.).

### Median Auto Electrician Salary from ABS Data

According to Jobs and Skills Australia (using ABS data from May 2025), the median full-time auto electrician earns **$2,808 per week** before tax. That translates to about **$46 per hour** based on an average of **49 hours per week**. This is significantly higher than the award minimum because it includes overtime, experience, and market premiums. The median for all occupations is $1,852 per week.

If you're negotiating an **auto electrician salary**, the median gives you a realistic benchmark. However, remember that 86% of auto electricians work full-time, and the average full-time hours are 49 – well above the 38-hour award standard. That extra time is often paid at overtime rates (150% for the first 2 hours, 200% after that).

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual auto electrician, your hourly rate must include the 25% casual loading. For example, the Grade 5 casual rate is $36.81 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave or redundancy benefits.

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual gross is $58,193 (award minimum), your employer must contribute an extra $6,983 to your super fund. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

### Tax on Your Auto Electrician Salary

For the 2026–27 income year, resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). Using the award minimum of $58,193, your tax would be approximately $9,779 plus Medicare, leaving about $46,500 take-home. For the median earner at $146,016 ($2,808 × 52), tax would be around $35,000. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the award minimum: $1,119.10 × 2 = $2,238.20 per fortnight. For the median: $2,808 × 2 = $5,616 per fortnight. This can help with budgeting.

### Key Takeaways

- The **auto electrician salary** award minimum is $29.45 per hour (Grade 5) for 38 hours.
- The median full-time auto electrician earns $46 per hour (49 hours) – much higher due to overtime and experience.
- Casual workers get 25% loading; super is 12% on top.
- Use the formula hourly × hours × 52 to estimate annual gross, then deduct tax.
- For a full breakdown, see our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data).

*Disclaimer: Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2027 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.*
